metadata.title: Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting: Developing Drugs for Prevention
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 27 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 28 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 29 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 30 not required. 31
candidates.context: This guidance does not address the development of drugs for the treatment of PONV. 23 Additionally, this guidance does not address the development of drugs for the prevention of 24 PONV in pediatric patients. 25

candidates.context: • Participants meeting the inclusion criteria recommended in section III.A typically receive 74 combination pharmacological PONV prophylaxis, which is consistent with clinical 75 consensus guidelines. candidates.context: Sponsors developing drugs for the prevention of PONV should consider the following: 72 • Trials should be randomized, double-blind, and controlled. Sponsors can consider an 80 active-controlled superiority or noninferiority 9 trial if an investigational product is 81 anticipated to provide greater or similar benefit, respectively, than the drug designated as 82 the active control within a standard-of-care combination pharmacological PONV 83 prophylaxis regimen. Sponsors can consider a placebo-controlled superiority trial, in 84 which all participants receive the same background standard-of-care combination 85 pharmacological PONV prophylaxis, if an investigational product is intended to provide 86 greater benefit than the standard-of-care regimen alone. 87

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the prevention of PONV should consider the following: 94
• To establish efficacy for the prevention of PONV, sponsors should assess the following: 98
candidates.context: 1. Efficacy Assessments 96 – A primary efficacy endpoint of complete response should be defined as no vomiting 100 and no use of rescue antiemetic medication in the 24 hours immediately following the 101 completion of the operative procedure. 102

candidates.statement: • Sponsors should analyze the primary endpoint (i.e., a binary endpoint defined as no 110 vomiting and no use of rescue antiemetic medication) and secondary endpoint (i.e., a 111 binary endpoint defined as no reported nausea and no use of rescue antiemetic 112 medication) by evaluating the difference in the proportions of responders across 113 treatment arms. 114
candidates.context: 2. Statistical Considerations 108 • Sponsors should adjust statistical analyses for baseline participant characteristics and 116 other related factors that may impact efficacy outcomes (e.g., age, female sex, history of 117 PONV and/or motion sickness, nonsmoking status, opioid administration) in order to gain 118 precision when evaluating overall treatment effects. Sponsors should also consider 119 exploring subgroup analyses and potential treatment interactions based on these factors. 120

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the prevention of PONV should consider the following: 130
candidates.context: D. Safety Considerations 128 • As trials of drugs for the prevention of PONV include administration of combination 132 pharmacological PONV prophylaxis, assessments of potential interactions between the 133 investigational product and coadministered drugs, including allowable rescue 134 medications, should be conducted early in development. 135

candidates.statement: • As trials of drugs for the prevention of PONV include administration of combination 132 pharmacological PONV prophylaxis, assessments of potential interactions between the 133 investigational product and coadministered drugs, including allowable rescue 134 medications, should be conducted early in development. 135
candidates.context: Sponsors developing drugs for the prevention of PONV should consider the following: 130 • Some antiemetic drugs have the potential to cause QT prolongation. The timing and 137 frequency of electrocardiogram assessments should be based on the arrhythmogenic 138 potential of the investigational product, as well as the arrhythmogenic potential of 139 coadministered drugs, including allowable rescue medications. Sponsors should consider 140 the potential for combined effects on the QT interval due to drug co-administration. 141
